dial.summary: BTC Accumulation thesis reinforced on Sep 4 with 5 of 8 indicators supportive: Global M2 expanding, 2s10s steepening to +40bps, Fed balance sheet stable at $6.73T, BTC funding near zero at +0.007%, and stablecoin dominance falling on a 30-day basis; three indicators neutral: ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6% (expanding but softening), DXY at 98.99 (neutral band), and real yields at 2.45% (flat 4-week trend); BTC.D has surged past 60% (60.15–60.66%, per BeInCrypto/AMBCrypto) burying near-term altseason prospects and reinforcing Bitcoin-first positioning; pivotal macro cluster ahead: NFP releasing today (Sep 4, consensus +53K), ECB decision Sep 10 (Reuters poll: expected +25bps hike to 2.50%), CPI Sep 11, and FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) held at ~$103.4T (July 2026 composite; ~6-week reporting lag means August aggregate unavailable until mid-October); June 2026 confirmed at $102.7T (MacroMicro); global broad money supply reached a record $150T in June 2026 (per Crypto Briefing, broader M3 measure); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23.22T (29th consecutive monthly increase, +5.4% YoY, record high); global M2 rose ~$0.7T over the prior 4-week window from ~$102.7T (June) to $103.4T (July composite); no YoY contraction from any major central bank; August global aggregate not yet published; 4-week uptrend confirmed (latest vs 4-week-prior composite); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); ECB Sep 10 hike decision and FOMC Sep 16 are the next key catalysts for global liquidity trajectory.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI released Sep 1 at 10:00 AM ET: 54.6%, down 1.0 percentage point from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion); below 55.2% consensus; Production 58.3%, New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp vs July), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp vs July); 4-week trend down: July 55.6% → August 54.6% = −1.0pp; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising, not met; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62, neither applies); TOPONE Markets preview notes August NFP and CPI Sep 11 are the remaining inputs before FOMC Sep 16; September ISM Manufacturing PMI (covering September activity) will be released on October 1—next reading; PMI at 54.6% corresponds to ~2.4% annualized real GDP growth.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 98.9871 on September 4, 2026 (StreetStats/web search aggregate), rounded to 98.99; 4-week trend down: DXY was approximately 100.3–101.4 in early August 2026 (late-July peak ~101.40 per Barchart; DXY at 99.60 tested channel support in mid-August per Barchart Aug 2026 technical analysis; fell to 98.55 during Jackson Hole week Aug 24-28 per Vantage Markets; bounced to 99.51 Sep 3, falling again to 98.99 Sep 4); relative change from ~101 (Aug 4) to 98.99 = −2.0%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; 4-week trend confirmed DOWN; status neutral (ICE DXY at 98.99 within 97.5–100 neutral band); structural dollar weakness driven by Treasury buyback program, weakening labor data (July NFP −23K), and rate-cut expectations ahead of FOMC Sep 16; ECB Sep 10 expected 25bps hike adds cross-currency pressure; a DXY break below 97.5 would shift status to supportive.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield): 2.45% as of September 2, 2026 (FRED H.15/FRED search confirm; next release scheduled Sep 4 2026 not yet indexed); 4-week trend flat: ~2.43% (Aug 4 estimate, per prior H.15 citations; Aug 10 confirmed at 2.43%, Aug 31 confirmed at 2.44%) → 2.45% (Sep 2) = +2bps, within the 5bps flat threshold; note: real yields declined to ~2.34% on Aug 27 (9bps August dip from Jul 25 2.43%) before bouncing back; status neutral (flat 4-week trend means 'rising AND above 2%' headwind condition is not fully met; 'falling or below 1%' supportive condition not met either); August real yield low was 2.34% (Aug 27, per prior H.15 citations); CPI Sep 11 and FOMC Sep 16 are the next catalysts for TIPS yield compression.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 4, 2026: 10Y yield 4.772% (Treasury.gov/web search), 2Y yield 4.371% (CNBC/web search); implied spread +40.1bps (+0.40%); 4-week steepening trend: ~+35bps (Aug 4 estimate per prior run) → +41bps (Sep 3) → +40bps (Sep 4) = +5bps steepening over 4 weeks; status supportive (positive spread AND 4-week steepening confirmed; spread moved from 35 to 40bps over the measurement window); FRED DGS10/DGS2 proxy-blocked this run—values sourced from secondary web search aggregates; curve-shaping events: NFP Sep 4, ECB Sep 10 (expected +25bps hike), CPI Sep 11, and FOMC Sep 16; ECB hike could lift long-end Treasury yields via global risk-off/rate-repricing, while a dovish FOMC would compress 2Y and further steepen the curve.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: ~$6.73T for week ending August 26, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 27); H.4.1 for week ending September 3, 2026 was released Sep 3 at 4:30 PM ET (federalreserve.gov confirmed via web search)—federalreserve.gov proxy-blocked this run, exact Sep 3 value unavailable; held at $6.73T as best estimate pending direct WALCL access (routine QT at ~$7B/week would imply ~$6.72T for Sep 3 week); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (early August) → $6.73T (Aug 26) = +$31B (+0.5%), within flat threshold; routine measured QT continues at stable pace with no acceleration or overnight rate spike; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau, QT pace stable); next H.4.1 with confirmed Sep 3 value is the only item needed to verify this estimate.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately +0.007% per 8h (web search, Sep 4, 2026; coinglass.com proxy-blocked); prior run: −0.0048% (Aug 28 verified observation); current: slightly positive at +0.007%, reflecting mildly bullish positioning as BTC price rose 4.77% to $81,044 on NFP day Sep 4; CoinStats AI Daily confirms Sep 2 BTC at $81,044.02; BTC.D has surged above 60% (60.15–60.66%, per BeInCrypto/AMBCrypto Sep 2026—BTC dominance breaking out of 8-month accumulation phase as capital rotates to Bitcoin from alts); 30-day trend flat: near zero or slightly negative throughout August, now slightly positive at 0.007% — a 10bps relative shift, within flat; well below the +0.04% per 8h overheating headwind threshold; status supportive (near-zero funding, no long-side overextension; spot-driven price action); NFP Sep 4 and FOMC Sep 16 are the next near-term catalysts for funding rate behavior.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$305B (Sep 4, 2026; CoinGecko search); total crypto market cap $2.7T (web search, Sep 4); stablecoin dominance 11.31% ($305B / $2.7T); BTC.D 60%+ (above 55% alt-rotation threshold—Altcoin Season Index at 37, per BeInCrypto/AMBCrypto Sep 2026); Bitcoin price ~$81,044 (Sep 4, up 4.77%); 30-day trend down: from ~13–14% (early August 2026) to 11.31% (Sep 4), a sustained decline of ~2pp over 30 days; the 30-day downtrend reflects capital deployment from stablecoins into risk assets, predominantly Bitcoin; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition—dominance rising while TOTAL also rising—does not apply as total market cap is roughly flat over the period); BTC.D above 60% keeps Alt Rotation signal firmly un-triggered; stablecoin market cap tracker shows $301.5B–$305B range across sources, consistent with our estimate.

upcoming.title: PPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—pipeline inflation read one day ahead of CPI August (Sep 11) and six days before FOMC Sep 16; July 2026 PPI was unchanged (final demand goods −0.7%, services +0.2%; per BLS archive); PCE for July 2026 came in at 3.7% YoY (released Aug 26); a cooling PPI reinforces the disinflationary trend and supports rate-cut expectations; a hot print alongside hot CPI Sep 11 would strengthen the case for a hold at FOMC Sep 16 and could pressure risk assets; released the same day as ECB rate decision (expected +25bps hike to 2.50%) and weekly jobless claims.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 6, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 6—penultimate labor read before FOMC September 16; week ending Aug 29 came in at 206,000 (slightly above prior week's revised level, per DOL); released same day as PPI August and ECB rate decision; a spike above 220K would reinforce the rate-cut case one day before CPI (Sep 11) and six days before the FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: ECB Rate Decision (September 2026)
upcoming.note: European Central Bank Governing Council rate decision at 2:15 PM CET (8:15 AM ET), press conference at 2:45 PM CET—released the same day as US PPI and weekly jobless claims; Reuters poll (Sep 3, 2026, per FXStreet) shows 65 economists agree the ECB will HIKE the deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.50%, a hawkish shift from prior expectations of a hold or cut; an ECB hike would support EUR/USD, add pressure on DXY, and could trigger global rate repricing ahead of FOMC Sep 16; hawkish ECB guidance risks a mild risk-off reaction in short-term risk assets before the FOMC decision resolves; the cross-central-bank divergence between a hiking ECB and a potentially cutting Fed is a key driver of DXY direction into Q4 2026.

upcoming.title: CPI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Consumer Price Index for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the final major inflation read before FOMC September 16; PCE inflation at 3.7% YoY for July (released Aug 26); the last leg of the data trifecta (NFP Sep 4, CPI Sep 11) shaping the September FOMC decision; a soft print below 3.3% would greatly increase cut odds and likely push DXY below 97.5 (supportive for risk assets); a hot print above 3.8% risks a September hold and Risk Off repositioning; also includes core CPI ex-food and energy; the ECB hike on Sep 10 adds cross-pressure—if ECB hikes while US CPI cools, the Fed-ECB divergence would be maximal and most bearish for DXY.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Survey preliminary read for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—released same day as CPI August; captures consumer inflation expectations (1-year and 5-year) alongside current conditions and expectations indexes; elevated 1-year inflation expectations would complicate the Fed's communication on Sep 16 even if headline CPI softens; a sharp drop in consumer confidence alongside weak CPI would amplify dovish expectations heading into the FOMC decision.
